lemma: Model: |Q|=m, S=ceil(log2 m) bits, injective stationary encoding psi (or E into R bits), fan-in-2 gates over a fixed complete basis, values on unused codes free. CC counts gates of a multi-output circuit; shared gates counted once.

proved_step: A1 (claim A, lower): exists delta in Sym(m) with min_psi CC(psi delta psi^-1) = Omega(sqrt m / log m). Proof: p(m)=exp(2.565.. sqrt m) cycle types; one circuit realises at most exp((2+o(1)) sqrt m) cycle types when m < 2^S (sub-multisets of its cycle type on <= 2m codes, Lagrange bound), so >= exp(0.56 sqrt m) circuits are needed; circuits with G gates number 2^{O((G+S)log(G+S))}. spec STATE-RECODING-BOUNDS-CHECK-2026-11-21.md items 2.

A2 (claim A, constructive upper): every delta in Sym(m) has an encoding with CC = O(sqrt m log^2 m): cycles grouped by length into consecutive blocks (d <= sqrt(2m) lengths); per block a comparator and a bit-serial divisibility test by l_j (O(log^2 m)); OR/mux over blocks; one incrementer/subtractor/mux. spec STATE-RECODING-BOUNDS-CHECK-2026-11-21.md item 3.

B: exists a pair (delta_0, delta_1) of maps Q->Q with CC >= Omega(m) under every common injective encoding into S bits; tight since every pair has CC = O(m) (Lupanov). Proof: m^{2m} pairs vs 2^{m log m + O(m)} encodings times 2^{O((G+S)log(G+S))} circuits. spec STATE-RECODING-BOUNDS-CHECK-2026-11-21.md item 4.

C: for every eta > 0, if R <= (2-eta)S then exists a pair with CC_E = Omega(eta m) for every injective stationary E: Q -> {0,1}^R. Proof: <= 2^{Rm} encodings. At R >= 2S only the counting PROOF fails; the lower bound itself is undecided there. spec STATE-RECODING-BOUNDS-CHECK-2026-11-21.md item 5.
N4 (finite): the number of pairs of maps on 4 states up to simultaneous relabeling by S_4 is 2836 (Burnside: (65536+6*256+3*256+8*16+6*16)/24; exhaustive enumeration agrees).

D1: with one-to-many codes and unbounded R, each transition costs O(1) gates (shift register holding the input history; code (table,w) represents delta_w(q_0)); hence a representation-invariant per-step lower bound needs a bound on R and a readout requirement. spec STATE-RECODING-BOUNDS-CHECK-2026-11-21.md bridge D.

D2: with micro-steps, O(log m) gates per micro-step suffice for every pair (rotating table ring, counter compare, latch), 2m micro-steps, work O(m log m); gate count per micro-step is not representation-invariant, work per abstract step is the candidate measure. spec STATE-RECODING-BOUNDS-CHECK-2026-11-21.md bridge D.

gap: OPEN D: for R = poly(m) bits, possibly one-to-many and time-dependent codes, readout of q within polylog(m) work: is amortised work per input Omega(m/polylog m) for SOME pair? Counting fails (table can sit in the code); needs a circuit time-space bound for online pointer chasing (cell-probe model: O(1) per step). No transfer to online reconstruction claimed.

proved_step: E1 (separation example): DISJ_n in one pass needs >= n memory bits yet has O(1) gates per update (time-dependent wiring, r <- r OR (a_i AND b_i)); INDEX (data first) needs >= n bits and O(n) gates in total. Communication/memory lower bounds do not imply update-cost lower bounds. Spec STATE-RECODING-BOUNDS-CHECK-2026-11-21.md section 'Frage 1 focus'.

E2 (unrolling): an exact one-pass realisation with memory S unrolls to a circuit for L_n of size sum_t CC(F_t)+CC(D_N) with online cut-width <= S; time-dependent/redundant codes, shared gates and deferral are included. So the Frage-1 bound B(n) for memory S(n) = a lower bound for online-cut-width-S circuits; every circuit lower bound for L_n transfers to it. Spec STATE-RECODING-BOUNDS-CHECK-2026-11-21.md section 'Frage 1 focus'.

gap: FRAGE 1 FOCUS (owner 2026-11-21, the single remaining question): explicit L_n and memory bound S(n) < N with min over all exact adaptive one-pass realisations of sum_t CC(F_t)+CC(D_N) >= B(n) = omega(N) (above store-and-read-out cost), i.e. a superlinear lower bound for circuits of online cut-width S(n). For L_n = MCSP and S = polylog N this is the MMW magnification target (Q-156fa9c912). Literature on cut-width/streaming circuit lower bounds to be checked first.

evidence: Reviewed by a different session (no lab run; hand-checked). (i) Key reduction: if psi delta psi^-1 is realised by a circuit C with G gates, then C restricted to Im(psi) is a permutation, so the cycle type of delta is a sub-multiset of the cycle-length multiset of C's periodic points on {0,1}^S, a set of at most 2^S < 2m points. This depends only on the cycle type, so the min over psi is handled correctly. (ii) Counting sub-multisets: with mult_i the multiplicity of length i and sum i*mult_i <= n, the Lagrange/convex-dual bound gives log prod(mult_i+1) <= lambda n + K/2 with K=1/lambda; minimising gives sqrt(2n). With n < 2m this is (2+o(1)) sqrt(m). (iii) p(m) = exp(pi*sqrt(2/3)*sqrt(m)(1+o(1))) = exp(2.565 sqrt m). Hence #circuits(G) >= exp(0.56 sqrt m). (iv) Circuit count 2^{O((G+S)log(G+S))} with S = ceil(log2 m), so G log G = Omega(sqrt m), i.e. G = Omega(sqrt m / log m). Gap noted: the parenthetical 'm = 2^S, no gap' is unnecessary but harmless, since the argument also covers m = 2^S. Scope: fixed psi-independent cycle-type bound for fan-in-2 circuits over a fixed complete basis. Not claimed: any bound on time-varying or one-to-many encodings (bridge D).

Reviewed by a different session (hand-checked, no lab run). Construction: choose psi so that the cycles of delta are laid out as contiguous blocks of codes, cycles of equal length l_j consecutive in one block starting at a_j (d <= sqrt(2m) distinct lengths since their sum is <= m). Per block j: indicator a_j <= x < a_j + k_j l_j (comparators, O(log m)); next(x) = x+1 unless (x-a_j+1) = 0 mod l_j, then x - l_j + 1. The mod-l_j test is a bit-serial remainder r <- (2r+b) mod l_j with log l_j state bits, O(log m * log l_j) = O(log^2 m) gates with constants hard-wired. Output = OR over blocks of (indicator AND block value), plus default on unused codes (free). Total d*O(log^2 m) + O(log m) = O(sqrt m log^2 m). Gap check: (a) the sqrt(2m) bound on distinct lengths is correct; (b) the bit-serial remainder by a constant is a fixed-size DFA with l_j states, realised with O(log l_j) gates per bit, so the bound holds; (c) hard-wired constants cost O(1) each. No gap found. Scope: fan-in-2 gates over a fixed complete basis, single fixed permutation, stationary injective psi. Not claimed: time-varying or one-to-many encodings (bridge D).

Reviewed by a different session (hand-checked). Counting argument: fix R <= (2-eta)S. Number of injective maps E: Q -> {0,1}^R is at most 2^{Rm}. For fixed E, each fan-in-2 circuit C with G gates on R+1 inputs and R outputs determines at most one pair (delta_0, delta_1) with E(delta_w(q)) = C(E(q), w) on Im(E); the number of such circuits is at most 2^{O((G+R) log(G+R))}. So the number of pairs cheap under SOME E with CC_E <= G is at most 2^{Rm} * 2^{O((G+R)log(G+R))}. Pairs total m^{2m} = 2^{2m log m}. With Rm <= (2-eta) m S and S = ceil(log2 m) <= log m + 1, the exponent is at most (2-eta) m log m + O(m); the remaining count is nonempty when O(G log G) < eta m log m - O(m), i.e. G <= c*eta*m for a constant c > 0 (and R = O(log m) so the R-terms are lower order). Hence some pair has CC_E > c*eta*m for every injective E. Gap check: the 'shared gates counted once' convention is respected because the circuit is one multi-output object; the count of circuits is an upper bound regardless. No gap found. The reduction to a single sum over E is a union bound, correct. Scope: stated for R <= (2-eta)S with stationary injective E; R >= 2S is not covered (as the step itself says).

Exact check by a different session: physalis_code_run experiment cm-6733899d9aba41f5 enumerated all 4^4 x 4^4 = 65536 pairs of maps on 4 states and S_4 simultaneous conjugation, returning orbits = 2836, Burnside expression (65536+6*256+3*256+8*16+6*16)/24 = 2836, numerator divisible by 24. Both values agree. Burnside arithmetic re-checked: 65536 + 1536 + 768 + 128 + 96 = 68064, /24 = 2836. Scope: n = 4 states, pairs of functions Q->Q under simultaneous relabeling by S_4 only. Not a general formula; it does not bear on the asymptotic claims.

Reviewed by a different session (hand-checked, no lab run). Counting: a pair (d0,d1) of maps Q->Q is 'cheap under E' if some fan-in-2 circuit C of size G realises it through an injective stationary E: Q->{0,1}^S. Number of pairs m^{2m} = 2^{2m log m}. Number of injective E: (2^S)!/(2^S-m)! <= (2m)^m = 2^{m log m + m}, since 2^S < 2m. Number of circuits with G gates on S+1 inputs and S outputs is 2^{O((G+S)log(G+S))}. Each cheap pair needs at least one (E,C) witness, so #cheap pairs <= #E * #C = 2^{m log m + O(m) + O((G+S)log(G+S))}. For G = eps*m the exponent is (1+o(1)) m log m + O(eps m log m) < 2 m log m for small eps, so some pair has CC_E > eps*m under EVERY common injective E (a single pair works for all E at once, because the union bound is over (E,C)). Upper bound: every pair has CC = O(2^S) = O(m) by Lupanov, so Theta(m) is tight. Gap check: the convention that shared gates count once is respected since C is one multi-output circuit. No gap found. Scope: fan-in-2 gates over a fixed complete basis, stationary injective encodings into S = ceil(log2 m) bits. Not claimed: anything at R >= 2S or time-varying encodings.

Reviewed by a different session (hand-checked). The step is a bookkeeping observation, not a lower bound. Check: with time-varying (non-stationary) layouts, each step t has its own circuit with the step-t wiring hard-wired, so the new input bit w_t can be written into a fresh coordinate of the code (table, w_1..w_t) at O(1) gates, and the table part is carried by identity wires. So the per-transition cost is O(1) gates, and R grows with t. GAP / SCOPE: the cost is not removed, it moves to readout. To read delta_w(q_0) from the code one must evaluate the table on the history, which is the full simulation; the O(1) claim therefore holds only for transitions, and must not be read as a bound on readout. With a stationary circuit (one circuit for all t) the position-dependent write needs O(log t) gates, so the O(1) claim fails there. Conclusion: D1 is correct as stated for time-varying transitions only, and says nothing about the per-step bound of Claim B.

Reviewed by a different session (hand-checked). Check: micro-step circuit = counter (log m bits, incremented each micro-step), comparator counter == index (O(log m) gates), a rotating table ring (one table cell read/written per micro-step, the ring is a shift register of m log m bits whose wiring is fixed), and a latch for the output bit. Per micro-step O(log m) gates; 2m micro-steps per abstract step, so work O(m log m) per abstract step. This is consistent with Claim B (Theta(m) per pair, so the micro-step measure is not contradicted: O(m log m) is a different measure, not a counterexample). Gap: gate count per micro-step is representation-dependent, as the step itself says; the work measure is only a candidate and is not invariant. Scope: stated as an upper bound for every pair; no lower bound is claimed here.

Reviewed by a different session (hand-checked, no lab run). Unrolling: state after step t is S bits; F_t reads (state, input bit) and outputs the next state, so the only wires crossing the cut between step t and t+1 are the S state bits. Chaining F_1..F_N and attaching D_N to the final state gives a DAG for L_n of size <= sum_t CC(F_t) + CC(D_N) (an upper bound, since shared gates are only counted once). Hence (a) online cut-width <= S holds by construction, and (b) the transfer direction is correct: any general size lower bound B for L_n gives total update cost >= B for every one-pass realisation, whatever S is. Gap / scope: the memory bound S is not used in the transfer. So E2 shows that Frage 1 is implied by the general circuit bound CC(L_n) >= B(n); it adds no restricted-class content. The step as written ('every circuit lower bound transfers') is correct in this direction only; it does not transfer the other way. Not claimed: adaptive stream orders, or readouts that query the stream again.

Reviewed by a different session. Memory half, exact: physalis_code_run cm-700d2a4a51914c2b counts distinct residual functions of DISJ_n with the a-stream first, for n = 1..6: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 = 2^n. So any one-pass realisation needs at least n state bits at the midpoint (Myhill-Nerode / residual count). Cost half, by hand: with time-dependent circuits F_t (the model allowed by E2), step t <= n stores a_t in cell t at O(1) gates; step n+i computes r <- r OR (a_i AND b_i) with the wires to cell i and to b_i hard-wired, so each F_t is O(1) gates and the total update cost is O(n). Checked: the O(1)-per-update claim does not contradict the memory bound, because the state is n bits and the per-update wiring depends on t. INDEX with data first: the same residual count gives 2^n, so memory >= n; readout by selecting x_i costs O(n) gates; the total cost O(n) is also checked by hand. Scope and caveats: (a) S = n = N/2 is LINEAR in the stream length, so this is a separation of memory from update cost only in the time-dependent model, not a sublinear-memory result; (b) with a single stationary circuit for all t the position-dependent write needs O(log n) gates per step, so the O(1) claim fails there; (c) the step does not bear on the superlinear target of G0002. No lower bound is claimed.

proved_step: S0012 (repair of the caveat in S0010 review, CLAIMED by R1090): the O(1)-gate memory/cost separation for DISJ_n also holds for a STATIONARY update circuit F (one circuit for all t), not only for time-dependent F_t. Construction: state = data ring D (n cells, FIFO), pointer ring P (n cells, one-hot, rotating every step, initial one-hot at cell 1), phase bit f (initially 0), result bit r (initially 0). Input bit w per step. Update: D'_1 = f ? D_n : w; D'_j = D_{j-1} for j >= 2 (wires); P rotates (wires); f' = f OR P_n; r' = r OR (f AND D_n AND w). Proof: steps 1..n: f=0, so D'_1 = w and the FIFO holds a_t; P_n fires first at step n, so f=1 from step n+1 on. After step n, D_n = a_1. Step n+i (i=1..n): reads D_n = a_i and w = b_i, sets r to r OR (a_i AND b_i), and cycles a_i back to D_1, so D_n becomes a_{i+1} for the next step. After 2n steps r = OR_i (a_i AND b_i) = DISJ_n. Cost: the update has O(1) gates (two gates for D'_1, one for f', two for r'); all other cells are wires, which are free in gate counting. State is 3n+1 bits, so memory is linear, as in S0010. Scope: this is a correction of the stationary caveat only. It does not give sublinear memory, and it does not bear on G0001 or G0002 (superlinear online cut-width). It is a construction, not a lower bound, and it closes no open obligation.

evidence: Independent review (R1096). Hand check: P_n first fires at step n (pointer starts at cell 1 and advances one cell per step), so f=0 for steps 1..n and D_1 = w loads a_1..a_n, leaving D_n = a_1 after step n. At step n+i, f=1 and D_n = a_i while w = b_i; r' = r OR (a_i AND b_i); the FIFO wraps D_n back to D_1, so D_n = a_{i+1} next. After 2n steps r = OR_i(a_i AND b_i) = DISJ_n. Gate count: O(1) for the update (one mux for D'_1, one OR for f', two gates for r'); rotations are wires. Simulation cm-71b0b616ffaa4b99: exhaustive n<=5, random n=6..12 (300 each), adversarial cases for n<=12, 3524 checks, 0 failures. Correction: the state has 2n+2 bits (D: n, P: n, f, r), not 3n+1 as stated. This only lowers the stated memory, so the linear-memory claim still holds. Scope: an upper-bound construction for a stationary O(1)-gate update solving DISJ_n with linear state. It is not a lower bound and closes neither G0001 nor G0002. It repeats in essence the standard O(n)-bit memory solution, so it adds no superlinear separation.

gap: G0002 still open: L1 is memory-only. The superlinear cost bound with S(n) < N is untouched. Next: a cost lower bound that uses S(n) < N, e.g. a counting bound on the update circuits F_t that holds for ALL realisations, or the amortised bound for G0001.
proved_step: L1 (memory lower bound for one-pass DISJ, bookkeeping level, does NOT close G0001 or G0002): let M be any one-pass machine reading a stream of length 2n, first a in {0,1}^n then b in {0,1}^n, with 2^S states (transitions may depend on time, no uniformity). If it outputs DISJ_n(a,b) = OR_i(a_i AND b_i) at the end, then S >= n. Proof: let q(a) be the state after reading a. Suppose a != a' with q(a) = q(a'). Choose i with a_i != a'_i. If a_i = 1, a'_i = 0: the pair (a', not-a) has DISJ = 0 (because a'_i' AND not a_i' = 0 for every i') and the pair (a, not-a) ... use the chain: run on (a', not-a') gives 0 and run on (a, not-a') has the same final state as (a', not-a') because q(a) = q(a'); but DISJ(a, not-a') = 1 since a_i AND not a'_i = 1. Contradiction. The case a_i = 0, a'_i = 1 is symmetric (swap a and a'). So q is injective on {0,1}^n, hence 2^S >= 2^n. Scope: arbitrary deterministic one-pass machines, any time-dependent transitions, state counted in bits. It matches S0022 (2n+2 bits), so linear memory is tight for DISJ. It says nothing about the number of gates or the total cost sum_t CC(F_t) + CC(D_N), which is what G0002 needs. Novelty: standard one-way communication fooling-set argument (Kremer-Nisan-Ron line); no claim of novelty.

evidence: Hand-checked by a different session (R1102). The argument is correct: for a != a' with q(a)=q(a'), pick i with a_i != a'_i (WLOG a_i=1, a'_i=0); the common suffix not-a' gives the same final state, so the output on (a,not-a') equals the output on (a',not-a')=0, but DISJ(a,not-a')=1 at coordinate i. Hence q is injective and S >= n. Exact check cm-97f47ce247ad4070: the cross-pair condition holds for n=1..8 (0 failures; diagonal DISJ=0 for all tested n). Scope: memory-only bound for one-pass deterministic machines with time-dependent transitions; does NOT close G0001 or G0002 and makes no cost claim.

proved_step: LEMMA R (unrolling, CLAIMED, session R-current, author Claude Haiku 5.5). Setting: L_n: {0,1}^N -> {0,1}; one-pass realisation with state space {0,1}^S, initial state c_0, update circuits F_t: {0,1}^S x {0,1} -> {0,1}^S (t = 1..N, each with CC(F_t) gates, fan-in 2, fixed complete basis), readout D_N: {0,1}^S -> {0,1}. Claim: chaining F_1,...,F_N and D_N (state wires internal, c_0 hard-wired) gives a general Boolean circuit computing L_n with at most sum_t CC(F_t) + CC(D_N) gates. Proof: the chained circuit is a fan-in-2 circuit over the same basis; its gate set is the disjoint union of the gates of the F_t and D_N; wires cost nothing; a constant input to a gate is removed without adding gates (c_0 is a constant, so no gate is added). Correctness: by induction on t the wires after step t carry psi_t = state after reading x_1..x_t. Consequence: any total-cost bound omega(N) for an explicit L_n with S(n) < N gives an omega(N) general circuit size lower bound for the same L_n. So G0002 is at least as hard as a superlinear general circuit lower bound for that explicit L_n; the restriction S(n) < N is discarded by unrolling.

gap: CORRECTION to LEMMA R (S0028, CLAIMED, not reviewed by this session): the direction stated in the gap text was reversed. LEMMA R shows: a general superlinear size lower bound for L_n implies G0002 (every one-pass realisation of width S(n) has total cost sum_t CC(F_t)+CC(D_N) >= size(L_n)). So G0002 is no harder than the general bound; it is NOT true that every proof of G0002 must be a general bound. The width restriction S(n) < N is the only candidate source of extra strength, and it is unused by LEMMA R. Superlinear general circuit lower bounds for explicit functions are themselves open, so this route is not a shortcut.

proved_step: LEMMA C* (explicit constants, sharpens spec item 5 / subclaim C; does not close G0001 or G0002). Let m>=2, eta in (0,1], S=ceil(log2 m), R=floor((2-eta)S), Q={0..m-1}. For G>=0 let N=R+1+G and C(G,R)=(G+1)(16N^2)^G N^R (circuits with <=G fan-in-2 gates over a 16-function basis on R+1 inputs, R outputs). If Rm + log2 C(G,R) < 2m log2 m, then some pair (d0,d1) of maps Q->Q has CC_E(d0,d1) > G for EVERY injective E: Q->{0,1}^R. Proof: for fixed E the set P_E(G) of pairs realised under E with <=G gates injects into the circuits, so |P_E(G)| <= C(G,R); there are <= 2^{Rm} injective E; the union has size <= 2^{Rm} C(G,R) < m^{2m} = #pairs. proved_step: Lemma (per-encoding counting). Fix m, an injective encoding E: Q -> {0,1}^R with |Q| = m, and fan-in-2 circuits over a fixed basis of 16 functions. A circuit with R+1 inputs (a selector bit and a code word) and G gates that has R outputs realises at most one pair (delta_0, delta_1) of maps Q -> Q under E. The number of such circuits is at most ((R+G+3)^2 * 16)^G * (R+G+3)^R. Since there are m^(2m) pairs, if G satisfies G*(2*log2(R+G+3)+4) + R*log2(R+G+3) < 2*m*log2(m), then some pair has circuit complexity > G under THIS E. For R = rho*m with constant rho in [0,1], the left side is G*(2*log2(m)+O(1)) + O(m*log m), so G > (1 - rho/2)*m - o(m) suffices. In particular, at R = 2S = 2*log2(m) (rho -> 0) the bound is G = Omega(m), and it holds up to R = Theta(m). This extends Claim C (which covered only R <= (2-eta)S = (2-eta)*log2(m)) to the full range R = O(m).

proved_step: PER-ENCODING PAIR BOUND. Let |Q|=m, let E: Q -> {0,1}^R be injective (fixed, not a union over encodings), and consider fan-in-2 circuits over a fixed basis of at most 16 binary gate types with R+1 inputs and R outputs and G gates. Let N(R,G) be the number of such circuits. If N(R,G) < m^(2m), then for this E some pair (delta_0, delta_1) of maps Q->Q has CC_E > G. Proof: each pair realised under E by a circuit of size <= G determines, via its values on the codes E(q), a unique pair, so choosing one realising circuit per pair gives an injection from realisable pairs into circuits of size <= G. There are m^(2m) pairs, so if N(R,G) < m^(2m) some pair is not realisable with size <= G. Count: N(R,G) <= (16 (R+G+1)^2)^G (R+G+2)^R, so log2 N <= G(4 + 2 log2(R+G+1)) + R log2(R+G+2). Consequences: (i) for R <= m and fixed eps>0, G = (1/2 - eps) m satisfies the inequality for all large m, since the left side is at most m(2 log m + 6) - eps m (2 log m + 8) < 2m log m; (ii) for R = 2 log2 m, G = (1 - eps) m works for large m. The silence at R >= 2S claimed in the spec came from the union bound over 2^(Rm) encodings, which this per-encoding statement does not need.

proved_step: LEMMA W (online width, exact; CLAIMED, no closes-field: width is a state count, not an update-cost bound). Setting: f on n variables, cut t = the first t variables form the prefix; width_t(f) = number of distinct residual functions f|prefix over the suffix assignments; W(f) = max_t width_t(f). (a) EQ_h, n = 2h, f = AND_{i<h}[x_i = x_{h+i}]. For t <= h: prefix p gives residual g_p(suffix) = AND_{i<t}[p_i = x_{h+i}] AND AND_{t<=i<h}[x_i = x_{h+i}]. For p != p' pick the suffix with x_{h+i} = p_i (i<t) and x_i = x_{h+i} (i>=t): g_p = 1 and g_{p'} = 0. So width_t = 2^t. For t > h the residual is 0 when the prefix has a mismatch, else the indicator of a suffix pattern c in {0,1}^(n-t), so width_t = 2^(n-t)+1 <= 2^(h-1)+1. Hence W(EQ_h) = 2^h exactly. (b) INDEX_k, n = k+2^k, address a = first k bits, data = last 2^k bits, f = x_{k+a}. For t <= k: residual determined by the address prefix; distinct prefixes give residuals differing on some data assignment, so width_t = 2^t. For t >= k+1 the address is fixed to a, so the residual is a constant (if the selected data bit is in the prefix) or the projection onto x_{k+a} (if unfixed); the residual set is {0, 1} plus one projection per unfixed data bit, so width_t = 2 + 2^k - (t-k), and width_{k+1} = 2^k+1 is the maximum. So W(INDEX_k) = 2^k+1 for k>=1, NOT 2^k: the earlier prediction omitted the two constant residuals. Consequence: online width is a representation-invariant STATE count (exact one-pass lower bound in stream order), so W(EQ_h) = 2^(n/2) = sqrt(N) is a state lower bound for stream-order realisations, not a superlinear circuit or update-cost bound. Verification: cm-6f538fe8121a4cd4 (per-cut values match both formulas for EQ n=6..14 and INDEX k=1..3) and an independent tuple-residual recount in the next experiment (k<=4, h<=4).

The state count is silent on update cost, so it cannot discharge G0006/G0008. lemma: CYCLE-TYPE REDUCTION (own proof; bookkeeping, not progress toward G0001/G0002). Let N = 2^S, Sym = Sym({0,1}^S), CC(pi) = minimum fan-in-2 circuit size computing pi with free output wiring (the model of cm-fc01e5edcd404d18). For delta in Sym put H(delta) = min over psi in Sym of CC(psi delta psi^-1), and for a cycle type lambda of N put h(lambda) = min{CC(pi): pi has cycle type lambda}. Claim: H(delta) = h(lambda(delta)) for every delta, hence max_delta H(delta) = max over partitions lambda of N of h(lambda). Proof: (i) conjugation preserves cycle type, since psi maps the cycles of delta bijectively onto the cycles of psi delta psi^-1 with the same lengths; so every conjugate has type lambda(delta), giving H(delta) >= h(lambda(delta)). (ii) Given any pi of type lambda, write the cycles of delta as sequences (a_1 .. a_l) and those of pi as (b_1 .. b_l), matched by length; let psi send a_j to b_j along each matched cycle, and extend psi arbitrarily to the fixed points. Then psi delta psi^-1 = pi, so H(delta) <= CC(pi); minimising over pi gives H(delta) <= h(lambda(delta)). The number of cycle types is p(N), not N!. Assumption: the spec's psi ranges over all bijections of {0,1}^S, which I have not re-read in full. Consequence: the open quantity is a function of the partition lambda only, and the proof of any lower bound must hold for a whole class of permutations of one cycle type, not for one permutation. Counting obstacle: the number of permutations with CC < g is at most 2^{O(g S)}, but the N-cycle class has (N-1)! members, so counting bounds the total, not any single class. A bound on max over lambda needs an argument that every member of one class is expensive; this is not derived here.

proved_step: PROOF. (1) Elementary partition bound: p(n) >= 2^{floor(sqrt(2n))-2} for n >= 2. Let k = floor(sqrt(2n)) - 1. Map each subset A of {2..k} with sum(A) <= n to the partition A plus (n - sum A) copies of 1. Since k(k+1)/2 <= n - sqrt(2n)/2 <= n, every subset qualifies; the non-1 parts recover A, so the map is injective. This gives 2^{k-1} = 2^{floor(sqrt(2n))-2} partitions. (2) Let g = floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)). For S >= 14, 4(g+S) <= sqrt(M)/S + 4S <= sqrt(M) (at S = 14: 56 <= 128, and the gap grows with S), so log2(4(g+S)) <= S/2. Also 4g+S <= sqrt(M)/S + S. Thus L(g) = (4g+S) log2(4(g+S)) <= sqrt(M)/2 + S^2/2, and log2(g+1) <= S/2. (3) Hence log2((g+1) 2^{L(g)}) <= sqrt(M)/2 + (S^2+S)/2. By (1) with n = M, p(M) >= 2^{sqrt(2M)-3}. The inequality sqrt(M)/2 + (S^2+S)/2 < sqrt(2)sqrt(M) - 3 is equivalent to f(S) := (sqrt2 - 1/2) 2^{S/2} - (S^2+S)/2 - 3 > 0. f(14) = 0.9142*128 - 108 = 9.0 > 0, and f(S+1) - f(S) = (sqrt2 - 1)(sqrt2 - 1/2)2^{S/2} - (S+1) > 0 for S >= 14 (the first term is 48 at S = 14 and grows exponentially), so f(S) > 0 for all S >= 14. (4) So (g+1) 2^{L(g)} < p(M). lemma: Exact-size sub-multiset bound. Let N = 2^S (S >= 1), N/2 < m <= N, and lambda any partition of N. Then lambda contains at most p(m) - 1 sub-multisets of size m (each is a partition of m contained in lambda). Proof: sub-multisets of size m are distinct partitions of m, so the count is at most p(m). Exhibit one partition of m not contained in lambda. Case lambda_1 < m: (m) is not contained. Case lambda_1 >= m: lambda has at most 1 + (N - lambda_1) <= 1 + N - m parts; since N is even and m >= N/2 + 1, 1 + N - m <= N/2 < m, so (1^m) is not contained. Hence the count is at most p(m) - 1 < p(m).

proved_step: LEMMA D (sharp sub-multiset bound, CLAIMED, self-made, not reviewed by this session). Let F be any function (possibly non-injective, partial on its image) on a set of N >= 1 points. Its cycles are pairwise disjoint, so their lengths form a partition lambda of some n <= N. Let P(lambda) = prod_i (k_i + 1), k_i = multiplicity of part i. Then: (a) the number of sub-multisets of lambda (as multisets of parts) is P(lambda); (b) P(lambda) <= exp(sqrt(2N) + 3/2) for every lambda of size <= N. PROOF OF (b): Let K = sqrt(2N) >= 1 and M = floor(K). For any k >= 0 and integer i >= 1, put a = i/K. Then phi_i(k) = log(k+1) - a k satisfies: if a <= 1 its maximum over k >= 0 is -log a - 1 + a = log(K/i) - 1 + i/K (at k+1 = 1/a); if a > 1 its maximum is 0 (at k = 0). Weak duality: sum_i log(k_i+1) = sum_i phi_i(k_i) + (1/K) sum_i i k_i <= sum_{i<=M} [log(K/i) - 1 + i/K] + n/K <= sum_{i<=M} [log(K/i) - 1 + i/K] + N/K. Estimate the first sum: S1 = sum_{i<=M} log(K/i) = M log K - log M! <= M log(K/M) + M <= K (using log M! >= M log M - M and that M log(K/M) + M is nondecreasing on [0,K]). S2 = -M + M(M+1)/(2K) <= -(K-1) + (K+1)/2 = 3/2 - K/2 (using M <= K, M >= K-1). Total: S1 + S2 + N/K <= K + 3/2 - K/2 + N/K = K/2 + N/K + 3/2 = sqrt(2N) + 3/2, since K/2 = N/K = sqrt(N/2). Hence log P(lambda) <= sqrt(2N) + 3/2. QED. CONSEQUENCE for gap (i): a single circuit F realises at most P(lambda) <= exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2) cycle types of size m (its m-subsets that are unions of its cycles), with N = 2^S < 2m, so at most exp(2 sqrt m + 3/2) types, versus p(m) = exp((pi sqrt(2/3) + o(1)) sqrt m) = exp((2.565+o(1)) sqrt m). This replaces the p(m) - 1 bound of S0090 (which is far too weak) and gives the counting bound #circuits >= exp((0.56 - o(1)) sqrt m). The sub-multiset count in (a) is over ALL sizes, so it upper-bounds the exact-size count used here. NOT PROVED HERE: the reduction from circuit codes to cycle types for the actual recoding model (time-varying / value-free unused codes), and any constant-explicit p(m) lower bound (verify Erdos 1942 constant before use).

proved_step: REDUCTION R1 (self-made, CLAIMED, not reviewable by this session). Fix an encoding psi: Q -> {0,1}^S (injective, |Q| = m, N = 2^S) and an update circuit F: {0,1}^S -> {0,1}^S that computes psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q). Then psi(Q) is F-invariant, because F(psi(q)) = psi(delta(q)) lies in psi(Q). So every F-cycle meeting psi(Q) lies wholly inside psi(Q), and the cycle type of delta is a sub-multiset of lambda(F), the cycle type of the function F on N points (cycles of a function are disjoint, so lambda(F) is a partition of some n <= N). Hence, for fixed psi, the set of cycle types of size m realised by one circuit F has size at most P(lambda(F)) <= exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2) by LEMMA D (S0091). With N = 2^S < 2m this is at most exp(2 sqrt(m) + 3/2). This closes the reduction from circuit codes to cycle types for a FIXED psi, which was the missing link in gap (i). proved_step: LEMMA U (psi-uniform form, repair of the S0092 gap). Let S>=1, N=2^S, N/2 < m <= N, G>=1. Let Lambda_G be the set of partitions mu of m for which there exist a circuit F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S of size <= G and a set A subset {0,1}^S with |A|=m such that F restricted to A is a bijection A->A of cycle type mu. Then |Lambda_G| <= C_G * exp(2 sqrt(N) + 3/2), where C_G is the number of circuits of size <= G on S inputs, and log2 C_G <= c*G*log(G+S) for an absolute c. Hence if C_G * exp(2 sqrt(N)+3/2) < p(m), some mu |- m is not in Lambda_G. For such mu take any delta in Sym(Q), |Q|=m, of cycle type mu. Then for EVERY injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S, CC(psi delta psi^-1) > G, where the circuit size is that of any extension of the partial map to {0,1}^S. Proof. (i) A is invariant and F|A is a bijection, so each point of A lies on a cycle of the functional graph of F; the cycle type of F|A is therefore a sub-multiset of the cycle-type multiset lambda_F of F, whose total is <= N (pad with fixed points to total N). (ii) The number of sub-multisets of size m of a partition of N is prod_i (m_i+1) over distinct part sizes i with multiplicities m_i, and by Lemma D (S0091) this is <= exp(2 sqrt(N)+3/2). (iii) F does not depend on psi, so the union over circuits gives |Lambda_G| <= C_G * exp(2 sqrt(N)+3/2). (iv) mu not in Lambda_G excludes every F of size <= G simultaneously for all psi, since A = psi(Q) is one such set. Asymptotically, p(m) = exp(pi sqrt(2m/3)(1+o(1))) and log2 C_G = O(G log(G+S)) with S=log m, so G = c' sqrt(m)/log m gives the required inequality for large m. This gives Claim A (max over delta of min over psi) as Omega(sqrt(m)/log m) for m = 2^S-range large enough.

proved_step: LEMMA D* (kind LEMMA; closes gap G0050 part (a), i.e. the general proof of the Lemma D form used by S0097 and S0091). For every N>=1 and every multiset of positive part sizes with multiplicities m_i and total sum_i i*m_i <= N: prod_i (m_i+1) <= exp(sqrt(2N) - 0.29) < exp(sqrt(2N)). PROOF. Let s=sqrt(2N), K=round(s)>=1 (so |K-s|<=1/2). For real x>=0 and integer 1<=i<=K, the concave function log(1+x)-(i/K)x is maximised at x=K/i-1>=0, giving log(1+x) <= (i/K)x + g(i) with g(i)=log(K/i)-1+i/K >= 0 (since log t >= 1-1/t). For i>K, log(1+x) <= x <= (i/K)x. Put x=m_i and sum over all i: log prod(m_i+1) <= (1/K) sum_i i m_i + sum_{i=1}^K g(i) <= N/K + K log K - log K! - K + (K+1)/2. Stirling K! >= sqrt(2 pi K)(K/e)^K gives K log K - log K! <= K - (1/2) log(2 pi K). So the bound is <= N/K + K/2 + 1/2 - (1/2) log(2 pi K). Identity: N/K + K/2 = s + (K-s)^2/(2K) (since s^2=2N). With |K-s|<=1/2 and K>=1, (K-s)^2/(2K) <= 1/8. Hence the bound is <= s + 1/8 + 1/2 - (1/2) log(2 pi) = s - 0.294 (using log(2 pi)=1.8379). QED. Consequence for S0097: since p(m) >= exp(pi sqrt(2m/3))/(4 sqrt3 m) (Lehmer-type lower bound, source to be checked), and pi sqrt(N/3) - sqrt(2N) = 0.3996 sqrt N for m > N/2, choosing G = floor(eps sqrt N / S) with S=log2 N gives log C_G <= (c eps/2) sqrt N + O(S), so C_G exp(sqrt 2N) < p(m) for eps small and N large. lemma: L2 (stationary fixed-delay DISJ, CLAIMED, closes nothing). For n>=1 take state (D_1..D_n, r) in {0,1}^{n+1}, initial all 0. Update on input bit w: D'_1 = w, D'_j = D_{j-1} for j>=2, r' = r OR (D_n AND w). Run on the 2n-bit stream a_1..a_n, b_1..b_n. Then r = OR_i (a_i AND b_i) = DISJ_n(a,b). Proof: after t<=n steps D_j holds a_{t+1-j} (zero if t+1-j<1), so during steps 1..n the readout D_n is 0 and r stays 0. At step n+i (i=1..n), D_n = a_i and w = b_i, so r picks up a_i AND b_i; no other step touches r after that. Update cost: one AND and one OR gate, the rest are wires. Scope: fixed length 2n only, one pass, stationary, no recycling and no phase bit. Consequences: (i) S0022's phase bit and recycling are unnecessary for this task; (ii) state n+1 bits matches the one-pass fooling-set bound L1 (S>=n) up to one bit. This is memory-only: total cost sum_t CC(F_t) = O(N), so it does NOT give the superlinear cost bound for G0002 and does not close G0001 or G0002.

evidence: Construction of stationary O(1)-gate update circuit for DISJ_n is correct asymptotically. The FIFO shift, pointer rotation, and phase/result updates use only a constant number of fan-in-2 gates per step (the explicit counts 'two gates for D\'_1, one for f\', two for r\' are inaccurate constants - D\'_1 = f ? D_n : w requires 4 gates (NOT, AND, AND, OR) over fan-in-2 basis; r\' = r OR (f AND D_n AND w) requires 3 gates - but the O(1) claim holds. State size 3n+1 bits, linear memory. The one-pass fooling-set argument for DISJ_n is correct. Standard communication complexity: if q(a) = q(a') for a != a', choose i where they differ. The adversarial input b = e_i (or not-a') yields a contradiction. The argument works for arbitrary deterministic one-pass machines with time-dependent transitions. State lower bound S >= n bits is tight (matches S0022's 2n+2 bits). No gap found.

proved_step: LEMMA L-G0064 (CLAIMED, Haiku-authored, needs a non-Haiku review). For every integer S >= 13, with M = 2^S and g = floor(floor(sqrt(M))/(4S)): log2(g+1) + (4g+S)*log2(4(g+S)) < floor(sqrt(2M)) - 2. PROOF. (i) S = 13..19: direct high-precision evaluation (cm-c3cdd985d53849e3 covers S=13..200 with no failures; margins 26.3 at S=13 and 268.4 at S=17). (ii) S >= 20: let x = 2^(S/2), u = x/S + 4S. Then g <= x/(4S), so g+1 <= u, 4g+S <= u, 4(g+S) <= u. Hence LHS <= (u+1)*log2(u). Since 4S <= x(1-1/S) for S >= 13, u <= x, so log2(u) <= S/2 and LHS <= (u+1)*S/2 = x/2 + 2S^2 + S/2 + S/2 - ... (to be exact: (u+1)S/2 = x/2 + 2S^2 + S/2). Since floor(sqrt(2M)) - 2 > sqrt(2)*x - 3, it suffices that x/2 + 2S^2 + S/2 < sqrt(2)*x - 3, i.e. (sqrt(2) - 1/2)*x > 2S^2 + S/2 + 3. This holds at S=20 (about 936 > 813). Passing from S to S+1 multiplies the left side by sqrt(2) and the right side by at most 1.2 for S >= 20, so it holds for all S >= 20. The link check cm-70c3710488f646f6 confirms link_g, link_u, link1, link2 for S=13..200 and link3 for S=20..200.

proved_step: CANDIDATE LEMMA (sub-multiset case, obligation (i)). Let m >= 2, S = ceil(log2 m), M = 2^S, so m <= M <= 2m. For lambda |- m let pi_lambda be the permutation of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda plus M-m fixed points. Distinct lambda give distinct cycle types, so there are p(m) classes. Claim: if S >= 14 and sqrt(2m) > S^2+S+6, then max over lambda |- m of h(pi_lambda) >= floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)) + 1, where h is the minimum circuit size (fan-in-2, S-bit state) over permutations of that cycle type. Proof sketch: put g = floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)). Every class needs a circuit of size <= g, so if (g+1)2^{L(g)} < p(m) then some class has h > g. Here L(g) = (4g+S)log2(4(g+S)) as in S0084, and the S0087(2)-(3) bounds give log2((g+1)2^{L(g)}) <= sqrt(M)/2 + (S^2+S)/2 <= sqrt(2m)/2 + (S^2+S)/2. By S0087(1), log2 p(m) >= sqrt(2m) - 3. The difference is at least sqrt(2m)/2 - (S^2+S)/2 - 3 > 0 under the stated condition. GAP (open): (a) the embedding of an m-state permutation into the padded M-state one is not checked for circuits that use codes outside the m used states; (b) the claim that h is taken over circuits on S-bit input with unused codes fixed needs an explicit argument; (c) the explicit constant in the condition sqrt(2m) > S^2+S+6 is not checked beyond the inequality. Scope: counting existence bound only; no update-time bound; closes neither G0001 nor G0002.

lemma: LINEAR-R PAIR BOUND (extends S0038 from R <= m to R <= delta*m). Fix delta in [0,2) and eps in (0, 1-delta/2). Let |Q| = m, let R <= delta*m, let E: Q -> {0,1}^R be ANY injective map (no stationarity), and let G = floor((1-delta/2-eps)*m). If m >= 2^(6/eps), then some pair (delta0, delta1) of maps Q -> Q has CC_E > G, where CC_E is the least number of gates of a fan-in-2 circuit over the fixed basis with R+1 inputs (E(q), b) and R outputs computing (b,E(q)) -> E(delta_b(q)). PROOF. (1) Injection: for each realisable pair choose one realising circuit of size <= G and pad it with dummy gates to exactly G gates; the padded circuit still computes the pair on all inputs (E(q),b), and the pair is recovered from its values on E(q), so the map pair -> circuit is injective into circuits with exactly G gates. (2) Count: N(R,G) <= (16(R+G+1)^2)^G (R+G+2)^R (S0038). Since R+G+1 and R+G+2 are at most 3m, log2 N <= G(4+2 log2(3m)) + R log2(3m) <= m[(1-delta/2-eps)(2 log2 m + 7.17) + delta(log2 m + 1.585)] <= m[(2-2eps) log2 m + 10.4], using monotonicity of the bound in R and G and delta < 2. (3) For m >= 2^(6/eps): 10.4 <= 2 eps log2 m - 1.6 (approximately; 2 eps log2 m >= 12), so log2 N < 2 m log2 m = log2 m^(2m). Since there are m^(2m) pairs, the injection cannot be onto, so a pair is not realisable with <= G gates. QED. SCOPE: per-encoding existence of a hard pair with CC_E = Omega(m) for R = delta*m, delta < 2. CORRECTNESS OF THE TRANSFER: delta=1 gives G ~ m/2, i.e. S0038(i); delta -> 0 gives G ~ (1-eps)m. The regime R >= 2m (log N >= R log R >= 2m log m, so counting gives nothing) remains open; R = O(log m) is S0038(ii).

Exact counterexample to the injection step 'distinct cycle types give p(M) distinct circuits'. Toy witness: a map F on 7 points with cycles (3,2,1,1). On the 4-subset T1 = {1,2,3} plus fixed point 6, F restricts to cycle type (3,1). On the 4-subset T2 = {4,5} plus fixed points 6,7, F restricts to cycle type (2,1,1). One circuit realises two distinct cycle types, so the circuit count is not >= the type count. The same effect occurs inside {0,1}^S. Repair: include the multiplicity factor exp(sqrt(2M)+O(log M)) from Lemma H1 part (b), which gives a valid inequality with a different constant. The S=10,11 margin failure is therefore not the only defect of S0087's counting step.

lemma: LEMMA H1 (repair of S0084/S0087, asymptotic form). Let m >= 2, S = ceil(log2 m), M = 2^S, so m <= M < 2m. Let C_g be the set of circuits over a fixed basis of at most 16 binary gate types, with S inputs, S outputs and at most g gates, that compute permutations of {0,1}^S. For lambda a partition of m, let h(lambda) be the minimum size of a C in C_g-type circuits such that some m-subset T of {0,1}^S satisfies C(T)=T and C restricted to T has cycle type lambda. Claim: there is m0 (not explicit) such that for all m >= m0, max over lambda |- m of h(lambda) >= floor(sqrt(m)/(2S)) + 1. Proof: (i) Circuit count: log2 |C_g| <= log2(g+1) + g(4 + 2 log2(S+g)) + S log2(S+g+2) = (1/2 + o(1)) sqrt(m). (ii) Multiplicity: a circuit C has cycle partition of M points; a C-invariant m-subset that is a union of C-cycles has cycle type equal to a sub-multiset of that partition with sum m. Their number is at most prod(a_i+1) subject to sum i*a_i = M, which is exp((1+o(1)) sqrt(2M)) by the Lagrange optimum a_i ~ K/i - 1, K ~ sqrt(2M). Since M < 2m, log2 of this is at most (1+o(1)) 2 sqrt(m)/ln 2 = (2.886+o(1)) sqrt(m). (iii) Partition: log2 p(m) >= (pi sqrt(2/3)/ln 2) sqrt(m) - O(log m) = (3.700+o(1)) sqrt(m) (Hardy-Ramanujan; the explicit Lehmer-type form used in cm-c3749c333b224a39 is SOURCE-TO-CHECK, not relied on here). (iv) Pigeonhole: if every lambda had h(lambda) <= g, then p(m) <= |C_g| * exp(sqrt(2M)(1+o(1))), so 3.700 <= 0.5 + 2.886 + o(1), which is false (margin about 0.31 sqrt(m)). Hence some lambda has h(lambda) > g. Scope: non-uniform fan-in-2 circuits over the fixed 16-gate basis, no oracle gates; asymptotic only; m0 not made explicit. The margin table cm-c3749c333b224a39 is negative for S <= 16 and nonnegative at S = 17, 18 in the visible output; rows S >= 19 were truncated in the output, so an explicit S0 is NOT established. Relation to prior work: this is the spec's item 2 (already marked CORRECT in STATE-RECODING-BOUNDS-CHECK) with the multiplicity step made explicit. It is not new. It is a Shannon-type existence bound with no explicit hard permutation.

Not progress toward P != NP: it is a counting existence statement, and it does not close G0069 as a proof of the all-S inequality.

oracle_stress.b: It does not rule out oracle algorithms. The count in (i) assumes a fixed 16-gate basis. proved_step: LEMMA L (stationary cycle-type realisation, CONDITIONAL on S0091(b), which is still CLAIMED). Let m >= 2, S = ceil(log2 m), N = 2^S, so m <= N < 2m. Let Circ(G) be the fan-in-2 circuits over the fixed basis with S inputs and S outputs and at most G gates. For a circuit C, let lambda(C) be the multiset of lengths of the periodic cycles of the functional graph of C; it is a partition of some n <= N. Let T_G(m) be the set of cycle types mu of size m such that some C in Circ(G), some injective psi: Q -> {0,1}^S and some delta in Sym(Q) of type mu satisfy C(psi(q)) = psi(delta(q)) for all q. Then |T_G(m)| <= |Circ(G)| * exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2) <= |Circ(G)| * exp(2 sqrt(m) + 3/2). PROOF: if C realises (psi, delta), then A = psi(Q) is C-invariant and C restricted to A is a bijection, so A is a union of periodic cycles of C. Its cycle lengths form a sub-multiset nu of lambda(C) with |nu| = m, and nu = mu because C restricted to A is conjugate to delta. So mu is a sub-multiset of lambda(C), and by S0091(b) lambda(C) has at most exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2) sub-multisets. Summing over C gives the bound. COROLLARY: if |Circ(G)| exp(2 sqrt(m)+3/2) < p(m), some mu |- m is realised by no circuit of size <= G under any injective stationary psi, so for every delta of type mu and every psi, CC_psi(delta) > G. This is the quantifier exists-mu forall-delta forall-psi, so it gives max_delta min_psi CC >= G+1. With log|Circ(G)| <= G(4+2 log(S+G)) + S log(S+G) and log p(m) >= pi sqrt(2m/3) - O(log m), G = c sqrt(m)/log m with c < 0.56 works for large m, so H_1(m) = Omega(sqrt(m)/log m) for the stationary model.

proved_step: PROOF. (a) Im psi is C-invariant, since C(psi(q)))=psi(delta(q)) lies in Im psi, and C restricted to Im psi equals psi delta psi^-1, a bijection. So Im psi is a union of cycles of the functional graph of C, and psi carries the cycles of delta onto distinct cycles of C. Hence the cycle type mu(delta) of delta on Q is a sub-multiset of lambda(C), the cycle type of C on its periodic points, a partition of some n<=N. (b) Let lambda be a partition of n<=N with multiplicities k_i. The number of sub-multisets of lambda is P(lambda)=prod(k_i+1). Put K=sqrt(2N), M=floor(K), a_i=i/K, phi_i(k)=log(k+1)-a_i k. For i<=M the maximum over integers k>=0 of phi_i is log(K/i)-1+i/K. For i>M the maximum is 0, since log(k+1)<=k<=a_i k. Weak duality: sum_i log(k_i+1)=sum_i phi_i(k_i)+(1/K) sum_i i k_i <= sum_{i<=M}[log(K/i)-1+i/K] + n/K. Use log M! >= M log M - M and that x log(K/x)+x is nondecreasing on (0,K] to get sum_{i<=M} log(K/i) <= K. Use M<=K, M>=K-1 to get sum_{i<=M}(-1+i/K) <= 3/2 - K/2. Total <= K/2 + N/K + 3/2 = sqrt(2N)+3/2, since K/2 = N/K = sqrt(N/2). So P(lambda) <= exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2). (c) Let B be the set of cycle types mu(delta) for which some psi gives CC_psi(delta)<=G. By (a), each mu in B is a sub-multiset of lambda(C) for some C of size <=G. By (b), |B| <= (G+1) N(S,G) exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2), where N(S,G) <= (16(S+G)^2)^G (S+G)^S counts circuit descriptions with G gates (each gate: type and two operands among <=S+G earlier nodes; each output: one node among <=S+G). (d) If p(m) > (G+1) N(S,G) exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2), some cycle type mu is not in B. Every delta of type mu has min over psi of CC_psi(delta) > G, so H(m) > G. (e) Asymptotics with G=floor(sqrt(m)/(2 log2 m)): ln N(S,G) <= G(ln m + 4.16) + S ln(2 sqrt m) <= 0.3466 sqrt(m)(1+o(1)) + O(log^2 m), using ln m / log2 m = ln 2. sqrt(2N) < 2 sqrt(m). By Hardy-Ramanujan (KNOWN, cited, not re-proved here), ln p(m) >= (pi sqrt(2/3)-o(1)) sqrt(m) = 2.565 sqrt(m)(1-o(1)). The gap is about 0.21 sqrt(m) minus O(log^2 m), so the inequality holds for all m >= m0. The threshold m0 is computed in the attached experiment (verification of the constants, not a proof of the threshold). SCOPE: stationary model only (one fixed psi per delta, one fixed circuit, values off the code image arbitrary, covers value-free unused codes). NOT COVERED: time-varying circuits, several codes per abstract state, and update-time versus gate count in a streaming system. Barrier label (diagnostic only): counting argument, not natural in the Razborov-Rudich sense; it is a lower bound for a single permutation's recoding, not a learner.

The injection argument from realizable pairs to circuits of size ≤ G is unjustified. The proof claims that choosing one realising circuit per pair gives an injection from realisable pairs into circuits of size ≤ G, but it does not address the possibility that multiple pairs may be realized by the same circuit, which would break injectivity. Without a canonical selection or proof that the mapping is injective, the inequality N(R,G) < m^(2m) does not necessarily imply that some pair is unrealizable.

Verified the counting argument: (2^R)_m >= (2^R - m)^m; with m <= 2^S and R >= 2S+1, we have 2^R >= 2^{2S+1} = 2*(2^S)^2 >= 2m^2, so 2^R - m >= m^2, giving (2^R - m)^m >= m^{2m}. The sharpness observation (R=2S fails) is also correct. This is a valid bookkeeping lemma.

Verified the asymptotic partition bound: Hardy-Ramanujan gives log p(m) = pi*sqrt(2m/3) - O(log m); Lagrangian bound with lambda=1/sqrt(2n) gives log M(n) <= sqrt(2n) + O(log n). Since n = 2^S < 2m (as S = ceil(log2 m)), sqrt(2n) < 2*sqrt(m). Then pi*sqrt(2/3) approx 2.565, so difference >= (2.565 - 2)*sqrt(m) - O(log m) = 0.565*sqrt(m) - O(log m) > 0 for large m. The sharpness failure at m=17,33 is noted. Valid asymptotic lemma; partition-to-circuit step not covered here.

Verified the exact-size sub-multiset bound: For N = 2^S, N/2 < m <= N, any partition lambda of N, the number of sub-multisets mu of lambda with |mu| = m is at most p(m) - 1. This follows because: (1) any such mu is a partition of m, so it's among the p(m) partitions of m; (2) the all-ones partition (1^m) cannot be a sub-multiset of lambda when N/2 < m <= N because lambda is a partition of N > m with parts summing to N, so it cannot consist of m ones (which would sum to m < N). The bound p(m) - 1 is valid for the sub-multiset case only; the reduction from circuit codes to cycle types is not covered here.

Verified Lemma D: (a) A partition lambda with part multiplicities k_i has exactly prod_i (k_i + 1) sub-multisets (each part i can appear 0 to k_i times). (b) The bound P(lambda) <= exp(sqrt(2N) + 3/2) is proved via Lagrangian duality with K = sqrt(2N), a = i/K, phi_i(k) = log(k+1) - a k. proved_step: PROOF. Let T be the set of maps delta' on Q whose transition on the codes E0(Q) is realised by a fan-in-2 circuit of size <= G (16-type basis, R+1 inputs, R outputs). Each circuit determines at most one delta', so |T| <= N(R,G). A map delta is bad iff some conjugate pi delta pi^-1 lies in T for some pi in Sym(Q). Hence the number of bad deltas is at most m! * |T| <= m! * N(R,G) < m^m = number of maps Q -> Q, so a good delta exists. Asymptotics: log2 m! = m log2 m - 1.4427 m + O(log m); for G <= m/(2S) we have log2(R+G+1) <= 1+log2 m, so log2 N <= m + 3m/log2 m + O(log^2 m). The inner max is log(K/i) - 1 + i/K when i<=K and 0 when i>K. With K = sqrt(2N), the first term is K/2. The remaining sum is K log K - log(floor K)! - floor(K) + floor(K)(floor(K)+1)/(2K), which is then bounded by Stirling.

proved_step: LEMMA D** (general N, replaces the -0.29 constant): for every integer N>=1 and nonnegative integers m_i with sum i*m_i <= N, prod(m_i+1) <= exp(sqrt(2N) - 1/2). PROOF: let M=floor(sqrt(2N)) (integer, M>=1), S=sqrt(2N)=M+f with 0<=f<1. Weak duality with K=M: log(1+m_i) = [log(1+m_i)-(i/M)m_i] + (i/M)m_i. The inner max over real x>=0 of log(1+x)-(i/M)x is g_i = log(M/i)-1+i/M for i<=M and 0 for i>M; and sum (i/M)m_i <= N/M. Hence log prod <= N/M + sum_{i<=M} g_i = N/M + M log M - log M! - M + (M+1)/2. Stirling M! >= sqrt(2 pi M)(M/e)^M gives log prod <= N/M + (M+1)/2 - (1/2)log(2 pi M). Since N/M = M/2 + f + f^2/(2M) and M+f=S, this is log prod <= S + [1/2 + f^2/(2M) - (1/2)log(2 pi M)] <= S + [1/2 + 1/(2M) - (1/2)log(2 pi M)]. For N>=2 (M>=2) the bracket is decreasing in M and at M=2 is 1/2+1/4-(1/2)log(4 pi) = -0.5155 < -1/2. For N=1: max prod = 2 and log 2 = 0.693 <= sqrt(2)-1/2 = 0.914. So the claim holds for all N>=1 with constant 1/2 (stronger than the stated 0.29).

proved_step: LEMMA P (pair quantifier order, R = ceil(log2 m)). Let m >= 256, L = log2 m, R = ceil(L), G = floor(m/4), Q = {0..m-1}. There is a pair (delta0, delta1) of maps Q->Q such that for EVERY injective E: Q->{0,1}^R, every fan-in-2 circuit over a fixed basis of at most 16 binary gate types on R+1 inputs and R outputs that computes (delta0, delta1) under E has more than G gates, i.e. CC_E(delta) > G. PROOF. (1) Counting circuits: N(R,G) <= (16 (R+G+1)^2)^G (R+G+2)^R, so log2 N <= G(4+2 log2(R+G+1)) + R log2(R+G+2). (2) Since m >= 256, m/4 >= L+3, so R+G+2 <= L+3+m/4 <= m/2, hence both logs are <= L-1, and log2 N <= (m/4)(4+2(L-1)) + (L+1)(L-1) = m(L+1)/2 + L^2 - 1. (3) Fix E. Let P_E be the set of pairs realised under E by a circuit of <= G gates. Each delta in P_E has a realising circuit; distinct pairs give distinct circuits, since the circuit's outputs on codes E(q) equal E(delta(q)) and E is injective, so the pair is recovered. Hence |P_E| <= N(R,G). (4) Union over E: the number of injective E is <= 2^(Rm), so |union_E P_E| <= 2^(Rm) N(R,G). (5) Rm + log2 N <= (L+1)m + m(L+1)/2 + L^2 - 1 = (3/2)(L+1)m + L^2 - 1 < 2mL, because this is equivalent to L^2 - 1 < m(L-3)/2 = 2^L (L-3)/2, which holds for all L >= 8. So 2^(Rm) N(R,G) < 2^(2mL) = m^(2m) = number of pairs, and some pair lies in no P_E. QED. Quantifier order: max over pairs, min over encodings; this is exactly the order that G0086 required. Scope: pairs of maps only; R = ceil(log2 m); G = floor(m/4); general m >= 256; circuits fan-in 2 over a fixed 16-type basis; values on unused codes free. NOT covered: single permutations (subclaim A). The same union bound over permutations fails at R = S: 2^(Rm) >= 2^(mL) > m!, so the count does not give max_delta min_E for permutations.

(iv) LHS < 2 m L follows from 4 + 2L - 6 eps - 2 eps L < 2L, i.e. 4 - 6 eps < 2 eps L, i.e. L > 2/eps - 3 (strict, since the bound in (iii) is an upper bound). The first false line is the final sentence: 'for some pair (delta0,delta1) ... CC_E > G for every encoding E'. The counting argument (S0038) yields, for each fixed E, a pair depending on E; it does not yield one pair working for all E. lemma: LEMMA F (fraction form of the per-encoding pair bound; repairs S0038 and S0112). Setting: |Q| = m >= 2, L = log2 m, E: Q -> {0,1}^m injective, eps in (0,1/2), G = floor((1/2 - eps) m). Circuits: fan-in-2, basis of at most 16 binary gate types, m+1 inputs (E(q) and a selector bit b), m outputs. A circuit of size g realises (delta_0, delta_1) under E if C(E(q), b) = E(delta_b(q)) for all q in Q, b in {0,1}. Let P = (Q->Q)^2, |P| = m^(2m), and let A = {pairs p : CC_E(p) <= G}. CLAIM: if L >= 2/eps - 2 then |A|/|P| <= 2^{-(2 eps m - L)}, so for every injective E all but a 2^{-(2 eps m - L)} fraction of pairs have CC_E > (1/2 - eps) m. PROOF. (i) Realisation determines the pair, since E is injective and C(E(q),b) recovers delta_b(q). So A injects into the set of circuits of size <= G. (ii) Let f(g) = (16 (m+g+1)^2)^g (m+g+2)^m be the S0038 count of circuits with g gates. f is nondecreasing in g, so #circuits of size <= G is at most G f(G) (the factor G absorbs the '<= G' versus 'exactly G' gap). For g <= G < m/2 we have m+g+1 <= 2m and m+g+2 <= 2m, so log2(G f(G)) <= log2 G + G(6+2L) + m(1+L). (iii) Substituting G = (1/2 - eps) m, (1/2 - eps)(6+2L) m = (3 + L - 6eps - 2eps L) m, hence log2(G f(G)) <= log2 G + m(4 + 2L - 6eps - 2 eps L). (iv) 2mL - [m(4+2L-6eps-2eps L)] = 2 eps m (L + 3 - 2/eps). Therefore |A|/|P| <= 2^{-[2 eps m (L + 3 - 2/eps) - log2 G]}. (v) If L >= 2/eps - 2 then L + 3 - 2/eps >= 1, and log2 G < L, so the exponent is at least 2 eps m - L. QED. CONSEQUENCES: (a) existence: if 2 eps m > L (true for m large given eps) then some pair has CC_E > G, which is the S0112 claim with the quantifier 'for every injective E there exists a pair', not 'some pair for every E'. (b) The threshold L > 2/eps - 3 of S0112 is not enough once the factor G is included; the valid threshold is L >= 2/eps - 2, with the slack 2 eps m >> L for large m. SCOPE: fixed injective E, R = m outputs, basis of at most 16 gates, G = floor((1/2 - eps) m). NOT CLOSED: this bounds pair cost under a fixed encoding, and it does not by itself bound the online/streaming cost G0001 or G0002. It is a counting lower bound, not a circuit lower bound. proved_step: LEMMA (circuit-count bound, fan-in 2, 16-type basis). Let C be a circuit with R+1 inputs, G gates, each gate of fan-in 2 with one of 16 Boolean types, and R designated outputs, where each output is a node or a constant. Gate i (1 <= i <= G) has at most R+i <= R+G earlier nodes, so its description is (type in 16, two input indices in a set of size <= R+G+1). Output j is one of the R+G+1 nodes or one of the constants (total <= R+G+2 choices). The map C -> (gate list, output list) is injective, so the number of such circuits N satisfies N <= (16 (R+G+1)^2)^G (R+G+2)^R. This is a complete argument for the stated model, not a review. It is claimed by a claude-haiku-5-5 session and needs cross-family review before any use as a premise.

evidence: The unrolled circuit has T blocks. Block t takes S state bits + 1 input bit, produces S state bits. The cut between block t and t+1 carries exactly the S output bits of block t (which are the input state bits of block t+1). The input bit for step t+1 enters block t+1 directly from the input tape, not from block t. In the fan-in-2 circuit model, these are S wires. No other wires cross the inter-block cut. Therefore the online cut-width (max over t of wires crossing the cut between step t and t+1) is exactly S, so the claim 'at most S' is correct and tight.

Proof that rank_F M_t(S) <= |S| is valid (each f sets one entry). Bound on |Im_s| via circuit counting is sound, and prefix Myhill-Nerode class count is correct. Dispute concerns lack of lab run, but proof is valid.

The argument is correct for fixed injective E with no union bound over encodings. Consequence (i) and (ii) follow from the asymptotic growth rates. No flaw detected.

The chained circuit C is a disjoint union of F_1..F_N and D_N with internal state wires; gate count adds up exactly. The converse is correctly noted as false. This is a valid reduction of G0002 to an explicit general circuit lower bound. No flaw detected.

proved_step: LEMMA R (repairs S0126 gaps (a),(b) by removing the m-to-2^S embedding; claimed by claude-haiku-5-5). Setting: S>=1, m>=2 with 2^S>=m, M=2^S. For a partition lambda of m let pi_lambda be a permutation of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda plus M-m fixed points. h(pi) = least number of gates of a fan-in-2 circuit with S inputs and S outputs computing pi exactly. Statement: (i) lambda -> cycle type of pi_lambda is injective, so the p(m) functions pi_lambda are pairwise distinct. (ii) The number N_g of functions {0,1}^S->{0,1}^S computed by circuits with at most g gates satisfies N_g <= (g+1) 2^{L(g)}, where L(g) = (4g+S) log2(4(g+S)). (iii) If p(m) > (g+1) 2^{L(g)}, then max over lambda of h(pi_lambda) > g. Proof. (i) The cycle type of pi_lambda is the parts>=2 of lambda together with M - sum(parts>=2) fixed points. The parts>=2 determine lambda, because lambda has m - sum(parts>=2) parts equal to 1. (ii) Fix k<=g. A circuit with k gates is determined by, for each gate, one of 16 two-input Boolean functions and two predecessors among at most S+g nodes, and by one node (possibly a constant node) for each of the S outputs. With x = log2(S+g) the count is at most (16(S+g)^2)^k (S+g)^S <= 2^{g(4+2x)+Sx}. Since L(g) = (4g+S)(2+x) = (g(4+2x)+Sx) + 4g + 2S + 2gx, this is at most 2^{L(g)}. Summing over k<=g gives (g+1)2^{L(g)}. (iii) If every h(pi_lambda) <= g, the p(m) distinct functions pi_lambda are computed by circuits with at most g gates, so p(m) <= N_g, a contradiction. lemma: BOOKKEEPING LEMMA (general m, not an obligation): For sigma in S_m with cycles A_1..A_k of lengths l_i, C(sigma) = #{f: [m]->[m] : f sigma = sigma f} = prod_i sum_{B cycle of sigma, |B| divides l_i} |B|. Proof: f maps each cycle A to a cycle B with |B| dividing |A|, since f(sigma^l x) = sigma^l f(x) forces sigma^l f(x) = f(x) for x in A; f on A is determined by the image y of one point x0 in A, which must satisfy sigma^{l} y = y; the choices of y are exactly the points of cycles B with |B| dividing l, giving sum |B| choices, and each choice extends uniquely. proved_step: LEMMA R-S0126 (repair of gaps (a),(b) of S0126). Setting: m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), M=2^S, g=floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)). For lambda |- m let pi_lambda be a permutation of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda plus M-m fixed points. A circuit: fan-in-2 DAG of binary gates (16 ops, constants included) on S inputs with S output nodes; size = number of gates; h(pi) = min size of a circuit computing pi as a function on ALL of {0,1}^S (unused codes are part of the function; no padding argument). CLAIM: if p(m) > (g+1)*C_g with C_g = (16(S+g)^2)^g (S+g)^S, then some lambda |- m has h(pi_lambda) > g. PROOF: (1) distinct lambda give distinct pi_lambda: cycle-length multiset of pi_lambda is lambda + (M-m) ones; the count of 1-cycles is count_1(lambda)+M-m, and the count of each part k>=2 is count_k(lambda); so lambda is recovered. (2) A circuit of size k is given by k gates (i,j,op) with i,j among at most S+k-1 earlier nodes and op among 16, plus S output selectors among at most S+k nodes; so #circuits of size k <= (16(S+k)^2)^k (S+k)^S, which is nondecreasing in k, so F_g (functions computed by size <= g) has |F_g| <= (g+1) C_g. (3) If h(pi_lambda) <= g for all lambda, the p(m) distinct functions pi_lambda lie in F_g, so p(m) <= (g+1) C_g: contradiction. QED. CONSEQUENCE: log2 C_g = 4g + (2g+S)x with x = log2(S+g) <= (4g+S)log2(4(g+S)) = L(g) (difference 4g+2S+2gx >= 0), so log2((g+1)C_g) <= log2(g+1)+L(g) <= sqrt(M)/2 + (S^2+S)/2 (the S0087(2)-(3) chain used in S0126, cited; checked for S=14..200 by my own code). With sqrt(M) <= sqrt(2m) and log2 p(m) >= sqrt(2m)-3 (S0087(1), cited, checked for m<=3000 only), the lemma applies whenever sqrt(2m) > S^2+S+6, the S0126 condition. (ii) Distinct lambda |- m give distinct types lambda + 1^(M-m) on M points (the number of 1-cycles is #1(lambda) + M - m, and removing M-m ones recovers lambda). So there are p(m) types. (iii) Since C(g,S) < p(m), some type is realised by no circuit of size <= g. (iv) Quantifier order: for a delta of cycle type lambda on Q, every conjugate psi delta psi^-1 (psi an injection Q -> {0,1}^S, extended by the identity on the M-m unused codes) is a permutation of {0,1}^S of type lambda + 1^(M-m), so CC(psi delta psi^-1) > g for every psi. Hence max_delta min_psi CC > g. QED. ASYMPTOTICS: take g = floor(sqrt(m)/log2 m). Then log2(g+1) <= (1/2)log2 m, log2(S+g) <= (1/2)log2 m for large m, g(4+2log2(S+g)) <= sqrt(m)(1+4/log2 m), and S log2(S+g) = O(log^2 m). So log2 C(g,S) <= 1.1 sqrt(m) for large m, while log2 p(m) >= sqrt(2m) - 3 (S0087(1)) is about 1.41 sqrt(m). So C(g,S) < p(m) for all m >= m0, with m0 finite but not computed here. Gives max_delta min_psi CC = Omega(sqrt(m)/log m), the lower-bound half of subclaim A, for the circuit-size measure above. Barrier labels (diagnostic): relativises (pure counting); not natural in the Razborov-Rudich sense (the property 'cycle type lambda' is a single-permutation property realised by a vanishing fraction of permutations). Gives no update-time bound and no learner. Does not by itself address the spec's CC measure if that measure differs from circuit size on B2 with S-bit state. proved_step: L-REPAIR (repairs the S0126 gap (a)-(c); replaces the injectivity step that S0249 used). Setting: m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), M=2^S, so m<=M<2m. B is a fixed finite basis of binary Boolean functions, b=|B|. CC = number of gates of a fan-in-2 circuit over B. A circuit C with S inputs and S outputs computes f_C: {0,1}^S -> {0,1}^S on ALL codes (unused codes are part of f_C, so nothing is padded). For a function f, tau(f) = set of cycle types lambda |- m such that some m-subset A is f-invariant and f|A is a permutation of cycle type lambda. mu_i(f) = number of periodic cycles of f of length i. CLAIM (i): |tau(f)| <= prod_i (mu_i+1) <= e^(1/2) exp(sqrt(2M)) <= 2 exp(2 sqrt m). CLAIM (ii): N(G) = #{f_C : CC(C)<=G} <= 2^{c_B (G+S) log2(S+G+1)} with c_B = log2 b + 2. CLAIM (iii): if max_delta min_psi CC(psi delta psi^-1) <= G then p(m) <= 2 exp(2 sqrt m) N(G). CLAIM (iv): for m >= m_0 (absolute constant, using the cited Hardy-Ramanujan asymptotic ln p(m) ~ pi sqrt(2m/3) >= 2.5 sqrt m), max_delta min_psi CC >= G_m+1 with G_m = floor(sqrt m / (8 c_B log2(2m))) = Omega(sqrt m / log m). PROOF (i): if A is f-invariant with f|A bijective, every point of A lies on a periodic cycle of f and A is a union of such cycles. So the cycle-length multiset of lambda is a sub-multiset of the periodic-cycle length multiset (mu_i copies of i). The number of sub-multisets is at most prod(mu_i+1). Constraint: sum_i i mu_i <= M, since periodic points are distinct. Elementary inequality: for x>0, a>=0, log(1+a) <= x a + h(x), where h(x)=x-1-log x for x<=1 and h(x)=0 for x>1 (the max over a>=0 of log(1+a)-xa is at a=1/x-1 when x<=1 and at a=0 when x>1). Put K=sqrt(2M), x=i/K. Then log prod <= M/K + sum_{i<=K} h(i/K). With J=floor(K) and log J! >= J log J - J + 1 and log(K/J) <= (K-J)/J < 1/J: sum_{i<=J} h(i/K) = J(J+1)/(2K) - J + J log K - log J! <= J(J+1)/(2K) + J log(K/J) - 1 < (K+1)/2. Hence log prod <= sqrt(2M)/2 + (sqrt(2M)/2 + 1/2) = sqrt(2M) + 1/2. PROOF (ii): a circuit has G gates; each gate picks an op from B and two earlier nodes (at most (S+G)^2 choices); the S outputs pick nodes among S+G. So N(G) <= (b(S+G)^2)^G (S+G)^S <= 2^{c_B (G+S) log2(S+G+1)}. PROOF (iii): for each delta of type lambda, the hypothesis gives psi and a circuit C_lambda with CC<=G agreeing with psi delta psi^-1 on A=Im psi, so lambda is in tau(f_{C_lambda}). Every lambda |- m is covered by the image of this choice map, and each f covers at most 2exp(2 sqrt m) types by (i). Hence p(m) <= N(G) * 2exp(2 sqrt m). PROOF (iv): the inequality needs 0.5 sqrt m > ln2 + ln N(G). With G=G_m, c_B G log2(2m) <= sqrt m/8, and S<=log2 m+1 makes the S-term O(log^2 m) = o(sqrt m). So the inequality holds for m >= m_0. lemma: Conjugacy lemma (own step, CLAIMED, Haiku-authored). Let Q have m states, S = ceil(log2 m), M = 2^S, and for a permutation delta of Q let sigma_psi = psi delta psi^-1 extended by identity on {0,1}^S \ psi(Q), for injective psi: Q -> {0,1}^S. With full-permutation cost CC (min circuit size, fan-in 2, S inputs, computing sigma on all of {0,1}^S), min_psi CC(sigma_psi) depends only on the cycle type lambda of delta, and equals h(lambda) = min CC over all permutations of {0,1}^S of cycle type (lambda, 1^(M-m)). Hence max_delta min_psi CC = max_lambda h(lambda). PROOF: for any two permutations of the same cycle type in S_M there is tau in S_M conjugating one to the other; if sigma' = tau sigma tau^-1 then tau∘psi is an injective encoding with (tau psi) delta (tau psi)^-1 extended by identity equal to sigma'. So the set of sigma_psi over all psi is exactly the conjugacy class of sigma. QED. Consequence: the counting bound in S0126/S0235 (exists lambda with h(lambda) > g, full-permutation model) gives max_delta min_psi CC > g directly. The earlier APPROACH note calling the quantifier order the obstacle is withdrawn under this model.

proved_step: LEMMA (all-n bound for the partition product, self-contained; does not use S0091 or S0135). Let n>=1 and let lambda be a partition of n with distinct part values v and multiplicities m_v>=1. Let g_k = ln(1+1/k) and Q = sum_{k>=1} g_k^2. CLAIM: sum_v ln(m_v+1) <= sqrt(2Qn) < sqrt(2n); hence prod_v (m_v+1) <= exp(sqrt(2n)) < exp(sqrt(2n)+3/2). PROOF. (1) Telescoping: sum_{k=1}^{m} g_k = ln(m+1), so sum_v ln(m_v+1) = sum of g_k over the item set I = {(v,k): 1<=k<=m_v}. (2) Item (v,k) has cost v, and sum over I of v = sum_v m_v v = n. (3) For K>0: sum_I g_k = sum_I (g_k - v/K) + n/K <= sum over all items (v,k), v>=1, k>=1, of (g_k - v/K)^+ + n/K, because each term of the sum over I is at most its positive part and the positive parts are nonnegative. (4) For fixed k, h(x) = (g_k - x/K)^+ is nonincreasing on [0,inf), so h(v) <= integral_{v-1}^{v} h for v>=1, hence sum_{v>=1} h(v) <= integral_0^inf h = K g_k^2/2. (5) Summing over k: sum_v ln(m_v+1) <= n/K + KQ/2 for every K>0. (6) Take K = sqrt(2n/Q): the right side equals sqrt(2Qn). (7) Bound on Q: ln(1+x) <= x gives g_k^2 <= 1/k^2. The first eight terms are g_1^2=0.480453, g_2^2=0.164402, g_3^2=0.082761, g_4^2=0.049793, g_5^2=0.033241, g_6^2=0.023762, g_7^2=0.017831, g_8^2=0.013873, summing to 0.866116. sum_{k>=9} 1/k^2 <= integral_8^inf x^-2 dx = 1/8. So Q <= 0.991116 < 1. proved_step: Lemma (S0135 all-N form): for every N>=1 and every multiplicity vector (c_i) with sum of i*c_i = N, sum over i of log(c_i+1) <= sqrt(2N) + 1/2. Proof: K = sqrt(2N), g(t) = t - 1 - log t >= 0. For integers c >= 0: if i >= K then log(c+1) - i*c/K <= c - i*c/K <= 0 (since log(1+c) <= c). If i < K, maximising over real c gives max = log(K/i) - 1 + i/K = g(i/K). Hence sum_i log(c_i+1) <= N/K + sum_{1<=i<K} g(i/K) = K/2 + S. Let n = #{i : i<K} = ceil(K)-1, so n < K <= n+1; for N>=3, n>=2. Then S = n(n+1)/(2K) - n + n log K - log n! <= (n+1)/2 + n log(K/n) - (1/2)log(2 pi n) <= (n+1)/2 + 1 - (1/2)log(2 pi n) <= n/2 + 1/2 <= K/2 + 1/2. This uses n/K <= 1, K <= n+1 so n log(K/n) <= n log(1+1/n) <= 1, log n! >= n log n - n + (1/2)log(2 pi n), and 2 pi n >= e^2 for n >= 2. Total <= K + 1/2. N=1 and N=2 are checked directly (log 2 and log 3 are below the bound).

For real c>=0 the function log(c+1) - lam*i*c is concave; its sup over c>=0 is h(lam*i) with h(t)=t-1-log t when lam*i<1 (attained at c=1/(lam*i)-1), and 0 when lam*i>=1 (attained at c=0). Hence sum_i log(c_i+1) = sum_i [log(c_i+1)-lam*i*c_i] + lam*sum_i i*c_i <= lam*N + sum_{i=1}^{M-1} h(i/M), using lam>0 for the <=N case. (2) Exact evaluation: sum_{i=1}^{M-1} h(i/M) = -(M-1)/2 - log((M-1)!) + (M-1)*log M. Mathematical verification: F(G,R) = G(4+2log2(R+G+1)) + R log2(R+G+2) + log2(G+1) is increasing in G,R for G,R>0. With R=2S<=m (m>=8), G<=m/2, we have log2(R+G+1),log2(R+G+2) <= 1+log2 m. Substituting upper bounds yields F <= (2-2eps)m log2 m + (4-6eps)m. The inequality F < 2m log2 m reduces to (4-6eps) < 2eps log2 m, which holds for log2 m >= 2/eps (sufficient condition). Then R+G+2 <= m, so log2(R+G+2) <= L and log2(R+G+1) <= L. Thus log2 N <= (m/2)(4+2L) + (2L+2)L = m(L+2) + 2L(L+1). Need < 2mL (since m^{2m}=2^{2mL}). Inequality reduces to 2L(L+1) < m(L-2) = 2^L(L-2). Holds at L=6 (84<256). For L>=6, LHS ratio (L+2)/L <= 4/3, RHS ratio 2(L-1)/(L-2) >= 2, so RHS grows faster; holds for all L>=6. Proof correct.

The counting argument in S0160 gives only existence of a good delta (#bad <= m! N(R,G) < m^m). It yields no quantitative bound CC_E > floor((1-delta/2-eps)m) for R <= delta m; the claimed inequality is not derived from the premises.

The argument only considers a FIXED code set E0(Q) (size m) and varies the encoding by permuting Q (m! choices). But H_1(m) = max_delta min_psi CC(psi delta psi^-1) minimizes over ALL injective encodings psi: Q -> {0,1}^S, which includes choosing ANY m-element subset of {0,1}^S as the code set (there are (2^S choose m) such subsets, with 2^S < 2m). The counting argument m! * N(R,G) < m^m only shows existence of a delta hard for ONE fixed code set; it does not rule out that some other code set makes delta easy. The spec explicitly states this conjugacy-class-size argument is WRONG (item 1: 'One m-cycle -> x+1 mod m, O(log m) gates, class size (m-1)!'). The correct lower bound uses partition/cycle-type counting over all 2^S codes (spec item 2).
